findings.title: Second `self.downsize` replaces the first, so `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` now raises ArgumentError
findings.body:
Ruby has no overloading. The `def self.downsize(from, to, dimensions, opts={})` at line 149 replaces the 5-argument version at line 145, which is now dead code. Its signature takes 3 required arguments plus 1 optional hash, so at most 4 arguments.

The existing caller `app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14` still calls `OptimizedImage.downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)` with 5 arguments. That raises `ArgumentError`, so the job fails and uploaded custom emoji are never downsized to 100x100. The other callers (`OptimizedImage.resize` in `lib/letter_avatar.rb:48` and `app/models/upload.rb:98`) are unaffected.

Fix: keep one definition. For example, name the new one `downsize_to(from, to, dimensions, opts={})`, or let `downsize` accept either `(w, h)` or a dimension string. Alternatively, change `resize_emoji.rb` to pass `"100x100"`. Add a spec for the job or for `downsize`; none exists today.

findings.title: Hard-coded 10MB client limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and caps admin-raised image limits
findings.body:
Before this change, `validateUploadedFile` read `max_<type>_size_kb`, so it applied `max_attachment_size_kb` to attachments. Now every file gets 10MB.

- Attachments larger than `max_attachment_size_kb` but under 10MB pass the client check. They are uploaded and only rejected server-side. The server also downsizes only images, so attachments get no such leniency.
- Admins who raised `max_image_size_kb` or `max_attachment_size_kb` above 10MB (for example `script/import_scripts/tnation.rb:115-116`) are now blocked client-side. The server would accept those files.
- Line 246 has the same problem for the 413 alert. It reports `10240` for any file type, even when the real limit is lower.

Fix: keep the setting for attachments, as in `type === 'image' ? 10 * 1024 : Discourse.SiteSettings.max_attachment_size_kb`. Better, use `Math.max(10 * 1024, max_image_size_kb)` for images. In the 413 branch, use the matching setting, not a constant.

findings.title: Downsize loop does not handle animated GIFs, SVGs or a failed conversion
findings.body:
The loop ignores the return value of `OptimizedImage.downsize`, which is `false` when the command fails (`optimized_image.rb:160-163`). It therefore always runs 5 times on a failing image.

For a `.gif` with `allow_animated_thumbnails` on, `optimize` switches to `downsize_instructions_animated` (`optimized_image.rb:137-138`, `155`). That emits `gifsicle --resize-fit 80%`, but gifsicle's `--resize-fit` expects `WxH`, not a percentage. I'm relying on my knowledge of gifsicle here and did not run it. The conversion would fail on every attempt and the oversized GIF would fall through to the validator.

`FileHelper.is_image?` (`lib/file_helper.rb:5`) also matches `.svg`. Running ImageMagick `-resize 80%` on an SVG, in place, rasterizes it or corrupts it.

Fix:
- Exclude SVG from the loop.
- Break when `downsize` returns false.
- Use a percentage-safe path for animated GIFs, or skip them.

findings.title: 10MB cap is not enforced server-side for multipart uploads, and the loop runs ImageMagick on unbounded input
findings.body:
The 10MB limit is applied only to API URL downloads (line 55) and in the client JS (`utilities.js`). A multipart upload takes `file.tempfile` unchecked, so the only bound is the web server's `client_max_body_size`.

The new block then runs up to 5 in-place `convert` passes on whatever image was posted. Each pass runs synchronously in a `Scheduler::Defer` thread, or in the request when the API passes `synchronous`. A user who bypasses the client check can therefore make the server do repeated heavy conversions on large files. Consider rejecting `tempfile.size > 10.megabytes` before downsizing, so the server enforces the same limit as the client.

findings.title: No tests for automatic downsizing or the new `OptimizedImage.downsize` signature
findings.body: `spec/controllers/uploads_controller_spec.rb` and `spec/models/optimized_image_spec.rb` have no case where an image exceeds `max_image_size_kb` and gets downsized. They have none for the `downsize(from, to, dimensions)` signature either. A spec calling the existing `downsize(path, path, 100, 100)` form would have caught the override at `optimized_image.rb:149`.

contracts.action: Upload controller downsizes oversize images in place before creating the Upload
contracts.equivalent_path: Upload.create_for resizes cropped image types in place via OptimizedImage.resize (app/models/upload.rb:98) and then runs ImageOptim
contracts.before_after: Before: images over max_image_size_kb were rejected by the validator. After: up to 5 in-place `convert -resize 80%` passes run first. Upload.create_for then re-hashes and stores the shrunk file.
contracts.visible_effect: Large images are accepted and stored smaller. The upload JSON, or the MessageBus message, returns the new Upload.
contracts.failure_mode: If conversion fails, the return value is ignored and the loop repeats 5 times. The Upload validator then rejects the file with a too-large error. Animated GIFs (gifsicle with a percentage) and SVGs are likely failure cases. The 10MB cap is enforced only for URL downloads.

contracts.equivalent_path: Existing caller app/jobs/regular/resize_emoji.rb:14 calls downsize(path, path, 100, 100, opts)
contracts.before_after: Before: downsize accepted (from, to, w, h, opts). After: the later 4-argument definition overrides the earlier one, so a 5-argument call raises ArgumentError.
contracts.visible_effect: Custom emoji are no longer downsized to 100x100.
contracts.failure_mode: Jobs::ResizeEmoji raises ArgumentError on every run.

contracts.action: Client-side file size validation uses a constant 10MB
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous code read Discourse.SiteSettings['max_' + type + '_size_kb'] for both images and attachments
contracts.before_after: Before: per-type limit from site settings. After: 10MB for every type, and the 413 alert also shows 10MB.
contracts.visible_effect: Attachments between max_attachment_size_kb and 10MB reach the server and are rejected there. Admin limits above 10MB are blocked in the browser.
contracts.failure_mode: The error alert shows a size that does not match the real limit for the file type.

summary: The PR adds automatic downsizing of oversize images on upload, but it should not merge as is. `app/models/optimized_image.rb` defines `self.downsize` twice, and the second definition replaces the first. The existing `Jobs::ResizeEmoji` call with 5 arguments now raises ArgumentError. The client's hard-coded 10MB limit ignores `max_attachment_size_kb` and caps admin-raised limits. The downsize loop ignores failures, and animated GIFs and SVGs probably fail it. No tests were added.
